summary: The Debian instructions deliberately don't put the PPA key in /etc/apt/trusted.gpg(.d), where it could sign any repository.
questions: Why not put the Ansible PPA key in trusted.gpg.d?

answer_card.title: Why the key isn't in trusted.gpg.d
answer_card.answer_md: A key in `/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/` or `/etc/apt/trusted.gpg` is trusted to sign releases from **any** repository. Keeping it in its own keyring and referencing it with `Signed-By` limits it to the Ansible PPA.
